label: q36-35b-lmstudio
note: LM Studio as its users run it: headless (llmster) with the newest runtimes, LM Studio's staff pick qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b (`lms get`), whose Mac variant is lmstudio-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MLX-4bit (the same shards as the MLX pack the other engines read), on the MLX engine. `lms load ... --context-length 32768 --parallel 1`: 32K like every engine (LM Studio's default 8192 is too small for the 16K prompt), one slot for parity (the default, 4, measured the same). Nothing else to tune: on these vision checkpoints the MLX engine has no speculative decoding (a draft model is refused, MTP is a llama.cpp/GGUF feature) and no KV quantization. Thinking switches off only through the hub model.yaml's enableThinking field via reasoning_effort none (chat_template_kwargs is ignored; a bare folder would think). LM Studio stops at max_tokens-1 (511 of 512), so decode runs carry a completion_tokens flag; rates use the reported count. Memory is the whole llmster tree (daemon + engine worker).

label: q38-27b-lmstudio
note: As the 35B: staff pick qwen/qwen3.8-27b, whose Mac variant lmstudio-community/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit is exactly the trunk the other MLX engines read (without the MTP head), MLX engine, 32K, one slot. Not measured: LM Studio's llama.cpp runtime on its Q4_K_M GGUF with MTP drafting, which could decode faster than its MLX engine on this model (standalone llama.cpp + MTP: 18.3 vs 15.3 tok/s) at a slower prefill.
